title: Light-minus-dark vapor pressure contrasts changed sign between August and September in a North Wales experiment in 2021
abstract: We tested whether a light-versus-dark actual vapor pressure contrast persisted across two complete months of a North Wales ozone and warming experiment in 2021. Heated-minus-ambient vapor pressure contrasts were lower in light hours in August and higher in September in all three heated domes. The primary contrasts were -0.061 to -0.048 kPa in August and +0.061 to +0.090 kPa in September. All four light rules, equal day weights and removal of any one day kept the monthly signs. Assumed independent reading errors of 0.2 C and one humidity percentage point permitted both signs in all 24 tests. These are error bounds, not confidence intervals. Prior work used the same records for pooled VPD and ozone overlap. This test adds a monthly phase check, not independent biological validation. One site-year, one dome per treatment, common ambient weather and unflagged gap filling limit inference. No plant response or physical drying mechanism is established. The package includes code, aggregate results, a figure and source retrieval instructions. External source and daily records remain outside the package.
